newsitem.title: GERMANY: BayernVerein 9-mo oper profit up 17.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: BayernVerein 9-mo oper profit up 17.5 pct.

text.p: Nine months to September 30 (in millions of marks unless otherwise stated)
Group oper profit after provisions 1,000 up 17.5 pct
Group net bad debt provisions 580.6 up 17.1 pct
Group own-account trading profit 189.8 up 4 pct

NOTE - Full name of the German bank is Bayerische Vereinsbank AG. Results compare with the first nine months of 1995. Analysts had forecast the bank would report operating profits of 990 million marks to 1.09 billion marks, after the bank reported a 24 percent rise in profit at the half-year stage.
Group net interest income 3,400 up 7.7 pct
Group net commission income 885.9 up 16.4 pct
Group oper profit before provisions 1,600 up 17.4 pct

NOTE - The bank said its parent operating profit after provisions rose by 29.4 percent in the period. Group commission income was boosted by strong capital market performance which helped its trust and securities business contribute 48 percent to its total net commission income. Mortgage business contributed 31 percent to net interest income. Spending growth slowed to 4.6 percent after 5.9 percent at the half-year stage. The rise was mainly due to spending on Advance Bank, Vereinsbank's direct unit. More details will be made available at a press conference today.
